title: API entity tags
label: TIKTOK SHOP · DEVELOPER GUIDE
subtitle: Updated 2026-07-01
html:
In the TikTok Shop API Reference, each endpoint is grouped under one entity tag. Entity tags help developers quickly understand:

  • The business entity that the API operates on, such as seller, shop, account, creator, or asset.
  • The data boundary of the API, such as seller-account data, local-shop data, account-level data, creator-account data, or asset-level data.
  • The authorization type required to call the API, such as a seller access token, creator access token, or partner access token.
  • Whether an additional encrypted identifier, such as shop_cipher or category_asset_cipher, is required.

Entity tags do not replace API scopes. Before calling an endpoint, check both the endpoint's entity tag and the required scope. For more information, refer to Access scope and Authorization overview.

Example of an API entity tag

Entity tag and access requirements

Use the following table as a quick checklist when choosing the access token and additional identifier for an endpoint. The exact API scope still comes from the API Reference and Access scope.

API entity tag Access token required Additional identifier How to read it
Seller Seller access token None for seller-level endpoints Use for seller account-level data and cross-shop operations.
Shop Seller access token shop_cipher Use for one local shop's products, orders, and shop-specific data.
Account Partner access token Usually none for account-level endpoints Use for account-level APIs.
Creator Creator access token None for creator-level endpoints Use for creator-owned data.
Asset Partner access token category_asset_cipher Use for partner campaign asset-level data, such as Affiliate Partner campaign data.

Ciphers used by entity tags

Some entity tags require an access token plus an encrypted identifier. These identifiers are not meant to be decrypted by developers.

Cipher What it identifies Required for How to get it
shop_cipher One shop that a seller has authorized for the app. Shop tag endpoints. Call Get Authorized Shops with a seller access token and use data.shops[].cipher from the response.
category_asset_cipher One partner business category asset authorized for the app. Asset tag endpoints. Call Get Authorized Category Assets with a partner access token and use data.category_assets[].cipher from the response.

If an endpoint is tagged Shop, a seller access token alone is not enough; the request must also include the correct shop_cipher for the target shop. If an endpoint is tagged Asset, a partner access token alone is not enough; the request must also include the correct category_asset_cipher for the target partner asset.

Text example of an API entity tag

If an API Reference page shows the Shop entity tag, read it as follows:

Item Meaning
Entity tag Shop
Data boundary One local TikTok Shop. Data is isolated from other shops under the same seller.
Access token Seller access token in the x-tts-access-token header.
Additional identifier shop_cipher, obtained from Get Authorized Shops.
Scope check The endpoint still requires its own API scope. Check the API Reference and Access scope.

Types of entity tag

Seller tag

Endpoints with the Seller tag operate at the seller account level. A seller access token is required to access the seller's data. These endpoints are mainly used to manage seller-level data that supports cross-shop operations. This includes seller-wide metadata, such as retrieving shops owned by the seller; reusable assets, such as uploading shop-agnostic images; and global product data used to replicate local product listings across multiple shops, such as creating global products. They cannot be used to access or manage individual local shop data, such as local products or a shop's orders. For local shop data, use a Shop tag endpoint with a seller access token and the target shop_cipher.

Shop tag

Endpoints with the Shop tag operate at the local shop level. A seller access token and a shop_cipher are required to access the shop data. Each shop has its own shop_cipher, and the data is isolated from other shops. These endpoints are mainly used to manage data within a shop, such as listing products in a shop, retrieving shop orders, managing local inventory, and so on. They cannot be used to access or manage data that spans across multiple shops under the same seller account. For seller-wide or cross-shop operations, use a Seller tag endpoint.

Account tag

Endpoints with the Account tag operate at the partner account level. A partner access token is required to access the partner's account-level data. These endpoints are mainly used for managing data related to the partner account, such as retrieving the list of business category assets that a partner has authorized for an app. They cannot be used to access or manage a partner's campaign assets directly. For partner campaign asset-level data, use an Asset tag endpoint with a partner access token and the relevant category_asset_cipher.

Creator tag

Endpoints with the Creator tag operate at the creator account level. A creator access token is required to access the creator's data. These endpoints are mainly used to manage data related to a creator, such as obtaining a creator's profile, retrieving affiliate orders generated by the creator, searching for open collaboration items, and so on. They cannot be used to access seller-owned shop data, account-level data, or asset-level data.

Asset tag

Endpoints with the Asset tag operate at the partner campaign asset level. A partner access token and the relevant category_asset_cipher are required to access a partner's campaign data. These endpoints are mainly used to manage affiliate marketing campaigns and handle campaign products. They cannot be used to manage the partner account itself, seller-owned shop data, or creator-owned data. For partner account-level data, use an Account tag endpoint with a partner access token.

Common mistakes to avoid

Do not choose an access token only by looking at the API path. First check the endpoint's entity tag, then confirm the required token type, cipher, and API scope. Do not use a seller access token to call creator or partner APIs. Do not use a partner access token to call seller shop APIs. Do not use a creator access token to call seller, shop, account, or asset APIs. Do not confuse seller-level and shop-level APIs. Seller tag APIs operate at the seller account level. Shop tag APIs operate on one local shop and require shop_cipher. Do not confuse account-level and asset-level APIs. Account tag APIs operate at the account level. Asset tag APIs operate on a campaign asset and require category_asset_cipher.
